messages:
maya: Heads up — got cert-expiry alerts flagged for eu-edge-01 and apac-ingress at ~02:03 UTC but when I pulled the certs they're still valid. Alerting system shows 'expiry' while cert-provisioner logs show KMS failures. Anyone seeing KMS/Decrypt issues?
aj: I grabbed cert-provisioner logs and saw KMS Decrypt denied around 02:02. Looks like the service account lost kms:Decrypt after the RBAC tightening earlier. cc @liam
liam: We rolled a SA->IAM binding change in the 01:45 deploy (pod-security-hardening). I flagged a rollback at 01:50 but thought it was limited. Paste the logs you have?
maya: log snippet: ```
2026-03-20T02:02:11Z cert-provisioner error: KMS DecryptDenied keyId=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111111:key/abcd principal=system:serviceaccount:certs:cert-provisioner
2026-03-20T02:02:11Z cert-provisioner info: queued cert request eu-edge-01 request_id=xyz123
```
aj: Also correlating with edge proxy metrics — nginx returned 495 SSL certificate error intermittently between 02:02-02:11. Trace ids: https://logs.redwood/trace/abc123 (filtered)
liam: k8s audit shows a SubjectAccessReview deny at 01:49 for cert-provisioner sa when it tried to call our iam-presenter webhook. CloudTrail shows KMS:Decrypt denied for that principal at same time. Link: https://logs.redwood/cloudtrail/2026-03-20?q=DecryptDenied
maya: Short mitigation: re-grant kms:Decrypt to cert-provisioner role, restart cert-provisioner pods, and temporarily increase audit verbosity for cert endpoints for 24h so we can collect forensics. Who can apply the change?
devops-sre: I can patch now. Proposed minimal policy: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111111:key/abcd", "arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:111111:key/ef01"]
  }]
}
```
I will attach to role cert-provisioner and restart pods in certs ns.
ops-bot: Runbook suggestion: revert RBAC commit 9f3b3 -> roll cert-provisioner pods -> validate cert issuance probe. Would you like me to execute (yes/no)? :robot_face:
maya: Yes please run it. Also capture `kubectl get events -n certs --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp` and `kubectl describe pod cert-provisioner-*-eu` and upload to the incident S3 bucket.
aj: Applied policy at 02:07, rolled pods at 02:09. cert-provisioner logs show successful Decrypt at 02:12 and certificates issued. nginx 495 errors dropped after 02:14. I'll attach brief evidence to the ticket.
liam: OK. Post-incident followups: 1) Authorize a least-privilege KMS policy as above and document key ARNs. 2) Add pre-deploy CI check for SA->IAM binding changes that validates KMS access with a dry-run cert request against a sandbox key in each region. 3) Add synthetic probe that fetches cert chain+hash from edge and ingest points daily and alert on chain mismatch/expiry delta.
maya: For the postmortem include: who approved the RBAC change, why the predeploy tests didn't catch it, timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (least-priv policy, CI guard, audit retention +24->30d for cert endpoints, canary checks).
aj: I'll open SEC-2026-042, assign to @maya @liam @devops-sre, and paste logs/commands. Quick commands I ran: ```bash
# attach policy
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name cert-provisioner --policy-name KMSDecryptForCertProv --policy-document file://kms-decrypt.json
# restart pods
kubectl rollout restart deployment/cert-provisioner -n certs
# verify logs
kubectl logs -n certs deployment/cert-provisioner --since=15m | grep Decrypt
```
devops-sre: Also recommended: add a CI test that runs `openssl s_client -connect eu-edge-01:443 -servername eu-edge-01` against a staging edge to validate cert chain and TLS config after any RBAC or policy deploy.
maya: Thanks all. Let's treat this as a near-miss — good catch. Assigning action items in the ticket. We'll keep audit verbosity on for 24h starting now and export artifacts to S3 for the security review. :thumbsup:
